question: What is the primary purpose of isolating a patient in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To interrupt the chain of infection
options.D: To shorten the duration of illness

explanation: Isolation physically separates infected individuals to prevent pathogens from spreading to other vulnerable patients and staff. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are isolation protocols especially critical in resource-limited Nigerian clinical environments?

options.A: Endemic outbreaks like Lassa fever require strict containment to prevent widespread nosocomial spread
options.B: Diagnostic testing is completely unavailable without prior physical separation
options.C: Hospital wards in the region are always constructed with negative pressure ventilation
options.D: Patients prefer staying in private rooms rather than open-bay wards

explanation: High-consequence infectious diseases can rapidly overwhelm open-bay wards if strict containment measures are not initiated immediately. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which category of infection control applies to every patient receiving care, regardless of diagnosis?
explanation: Standard precautions are universal measures applied to all patients because infection status is not always immediately known. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: When must transmission-based precautions be initiated for a hospitalized client?

options.A: When the patient requests a private room for personal comfort
options.B: As soon as an infection with a specific route of spread is suspected or confirmed
options.C: Immediately upon discharge from the emergency department
options.D: Only after laboratory culture results return positive after seven days

explanation: Waiting for lab confirmation can cause delayed containment; precautions must start empirically based on clinical presentation and suspected pathogen. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which type of transmission-based precaution requires the use of a fitted N95 respirator mask?
explanation: Airborne pathogens travel via droplet nuclei that stay suspended in the air, necessitating high-efficiency particulate filtration masks like the N95. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which specific infection control measure is mandatory?

options.A: Putting a simple cloth mask on the nurse only during medication administration
options.B: Placement in a negative pressure room with airborne precautions
options.C: Isolating the client using contact precautions and sterile gloves
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent droplet formation

explanation: Active tuberculosis is airborne, requiring both a negative pressure environment and respiratory protection to safeguard staff and other patients. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the very first item of personal protective equipment that should be removed during doffing?
explanation: Gloves are typically the most heavily contaminated item and must be peeled off first to prevent transferring pathogens to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is performing hand hygiene between removing individual pieces of personal protective equipment critical?

options.A: It helps preserve the structural integrity of the remaining protective equipment
options.B: It complies with facility laundering schedules for reusable gowns
options.C: It prevents accidental self-contamination if hands touch a contaminated surface during removal
options.D: It reduces skin dryness caused by prolonged glove wear

explanation: Touching the outside of gowns or face shields during removal often transfers microbes to the hands, making intermediate hand hygiene essential. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the direction of airflow when a negative pressure isolation room door is opened?

options.A: Inward from the hallway into the room
options.B: Directly upward through the ceiling tiles
options.C: Circular throughout the immediate doorway threshold
options.D: Outward from the room into the hallway

explanation: Negative pressure creates lower air pressure inside the room, causing air to rush inward and trap airborne pathogens inside. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h5)

question: For which type of patient is a positive pressure isolation room primarily indicated?

options.A: An individual diagnosed with severe cholera
options.B: A patient recovering from uncomplicated malaria
options.C: A client with active pulmonary tuberculosis

explanation: Positive pressure pushes air outward, preventing dust and airborne pathogens from entering the room and infecting a susceptible patient. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which psychological response is most commonly observed in patients placed under strict isolation precautions?
explanation: Sensory deprivation and separation from loved ones frequently cause isolated patients to experience heightened anxiety and depressive symptoms. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)

question: How can a nurse best address the emotional needs of a patient experiencing prolonged isolation?

options.A: Provide regular communication, clear explanations, and facilitated contact with family
options.B: Limit room entry entirely to prevent any conversation with the client
options.C: Administer routine sedatives to keep the client asleep throughout the day
options.D: Discourage visitors permanently to maintain absolute environmental sterility

explanation: Active engagement, reassurance, and alternative communication methods preserve mental well-being without compromising infection control. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is a key responsibility of the community health nurse during a suspected infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: Conducting contact tracing and community health education
options.B: Closing all primary healthcare clinics indefinitely
options.C: Constructing negative pressure ventilation systems in rural homes
options.D: Manufacturing personal protective equipment locally without guidelines

explanation: Community nurses track exposed individuals and educate the public on prevention, forming the backbone of local epidemic control. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which action is MOST appropriate when advising a family caring for an infectious patient at home in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: Advise the family to burn all contaminated linen and medical waste inside the living room
options.B: Designate a specific separate room for the patient and educate caregivers on safe waste management
options.C: Instruct all family members to share the same sleeping quarters to monitor symptoms closely
options.D: Tell the caregivers that standard soap and water are completely ineffective for hand hygiene

explanation: Practical home isolation relies on spatial separation and clear instructions on safe handling of excretions and waste. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h7)
